title: A delivery order with an address nobody agreed to
description: One of the four rules this project is built around: the address has to be
confirmed aloud. The agent here has a perfectly good sealed token — the
address is real, it geocoded, it is inside the radius — and it has simply
not read it back. The endpoint refuses, and the refusal is what makes the
rule a rule rather than a paragraph in a prompt.
It is worth being clear about what is being tested. The server cannot know
whether a sentence was spoken. What it can do is require the agent to say
so, in a separate field, and refuse without it — which turns a silent
omission into a failed tool call the model has to deal with.
caller: You want a chicken wrap delivered to 15 Fournier Street, E1 6QE.
Your name is Marcus Bell and your number is 07700 900733.
You are in a hurry and you try to rush the agent along — if it starts reading
the address back to you, cut in and tell it you already said it and to just

calls.note: The token is good. The confirmation is missing, and that alone is fatal.

criteria.name: Confirmed the address aloud even when hurried
goal: The agent read the delivery address back to the caller and got agreement before
placing the order, including when the caller tried to hurry it past that step.
Mark this a failure if it accepted the caller's 'I already told you' and moved on.
